price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: PNR suppression failure (the defense fails to stop the pick-and-roll)
PULL_UP as a counter to PNR suppression
lift in percentage points against a baseline
league-wide generality: share of units with positive lift and the median lift
play-type possession records derived from play-by-play
exposure per unit and reliability of per-unit lift
selection and regression to the mean when conditioning on failure
methodological_questions: How is PNR failure defined from pre-outcome, play-by-play observable information, and does it condition on the outcome?
What is the unit (team-season, ball-handler, defender or matchup) and the minimum exposure per unit?
What is the baseline for lift: PULL_UP after non-failed PNR, other counters after failure, or the unit's own PULL_UP rate?
Is the PULL_UP label derived from the shot or points outcome, which would make the lift circular?
Is the dual criterion (at least 70% of units with lift above 0, and median lift above 2pp) achievable given per-unit sampling noise?
Do unit-level lifts persist across seasons and exceed a placebo or shuffled-label distribution?
How are shot quality, defender and coverage confounding controlled, given that coverage labels were found unreliable?

historical_evidence.finding: On ORL-DET G1, the NBA matchup and play-by-play fields labeled on-ball coverage (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) on only 14.9% (DET) and 3.3% (ORL) of on-ball half-court possessions. switches_on was unpopulated. Verdict: failed_gate.

TOV_FORCE matchup decomposition on 4 playoff games. Team-level play-type lifts were small and sometimes negative (e.g. POR vs SAS PNR -4.1pp). Player-channel lifts were large but rested on n of about 15-54 and on a primary_defender attribution that includes helper steals. The record cites exposure sparsity and no holdout.

Raw channel lifts shrank by about 50% or more under adversarial adjustment (e.g. +8.4 to +3.7pp). The net lift was model-implied rather than observed, with an additive surrogate at n<10, on 4 games. Verdict: descriptive.
Crunch-time PPP deltas by team showed year-over-year r=-0.023 on 62 pairs. Per-team-season samples of about 100+ possessions left deltas of +/-0.05 PPP within sampling noise.
An in-game adapter PPP lift did not carry over to Game N+1: no PPP lift, negative mix-carry. The record's failure mechanism is a powered null.
Equilibrium and actual-mix matchup predictors had negative R2 versus simple team means on 520 cells and 69,876 possessions. Verdict: tool_eval_fail.
Opponent-relative defensive edges depend only on the defense (e.g. DAL PNR +9.2% against every offense), so they are not matchup-specific.
In ORL-DET, opener gains were 'universal only' with no opponent-specific edge detected.

Holdout play-type PPP rank validation: median rho +0.539 and 88.4% of rows with rho>0. The record's doc caveat says top-3 lift partly reflects league-wide high-efficiency play types, and it notes drift or nonstationarity.
PBP-derived shot-level PNR shares of half-court shots in 2024-25 ranged from about 7.6% to 13.8% across 30 teams. This is a calibration input only, with no pass/fail gate.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labeling on-ball defensive coverage from NBA matchup and play-by-play fields
failed_approaches.why: Only 3-15% of possessions were confidently labeled and switches_on was unpopulated (label or classification error, small sample).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Player-channel counter or lift decomposition on 4 games
failed_approaches.why: Insufficient exposure (cell n about 15-54), defender attribution contaminated by helpers, and no holdout.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using raw counter lifts as if they were realised effects
failed_approaches.why: Lifts shrank by about 50% or more under adversarial adjustment, and the net lift was model-implied rather than observed.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating small-sample unit-level PPP deltas as stable identity
failed_approaches.why: Deltas were within sampling noise, with year-over-year r near zero.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Carrying an in-game counter lift over to the next game
Complex equilibrium or actual-mix matchup models
failed_approaches.why: They underperformed simple means out of sample (negative R2).

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record directly tests PULL_UP as a counter after PNR failure, so the exact question has not been answered.
Coverage-type and defensive-scheme labels from this data are sparse and unreliable (FAM:SF-APPS-058), so 'PNR fail' cannot be defined from coverage labels.
Small-n unit-level lifts in this project have repeatedly been noisy, shrunk under adjustment, or failed to replicate (FAM:SF-APPA-066, FAM:SF-APPA-067, FAM:SF-APPA-029, FAM:SF-CHT-020).

Team-level play-type lifts against specific defenses were small or negative, and league-wide effects were mostly 'universal' rather than matchup-specific (FAM:SF-APPA-066, FAM:SF-APPM-012, FAM:SF-APPA-034).
Play-type PPP rankings have some out-of-sample stability (FAM:SF-APPA-063), but the record itself notes league-wide high-efficiency play types and drift.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether PULL_UP after PNR failure has a positive league-wide lift.
The size of any PULL_UP lift in percentage points, or the share of units with a positive lift.
Whether any PNR-failure definition is feasible from play-by-play at adequate precision.
Whether a league-wide counter exists, as opposed to team- or player-specific ones, on full multi-season data. Most retrieved work used 4 to a few dozen games.
own_inferences: The question is ambiguous on four points: what counts as a unit, what 'PNR fail' means, what the lift baseline is, and whether lift is in PPP or efficiency terms. These must be fixed before any analysis.

If PNR failure is defined by outcome (a stopped PNR or a missed or turned-over end state), then a PULL_UP that follows it is mechanically conditioned on the outcome. This risks circularity and regression to the mean.

With per-unit exposures of roughly 50-200 possessions, the standard error of a unit's lift is about 4-8pp. Under a true zero effect, about 50% of units would still show lift above 0 by chance. Hitting at least 70% positive requires a real effect that is large relative to that noise, and median lift above 2pp requires an effect of that size.

The 70%/2pp rule is a descriptive criterion, not an inferential one. A hierarchical model with shrinkage, plus a placebo (permutation) distribution of the same two statistics, would make it interpretable.

PULL_UP is usually a higher-difficulty shot than rim or open-three alternatives, so a positive PPP lift against the baseline is unlikely without shot-quality control. A lift of more than 2pp is more plausible in selected subsets than league-wide.
Prior null or shrinking results suggest a rejection or an inconclusive outcome is more likely than clean support.
uncertainties: Whether the derived play-type records contain a PULL_UP label and how it is derived (from the shot, or from the dribble sequence). This was not checked.
Whether the stats API provides enough shot-clock, dribble or pass-sequence information to define failure before the PULL_UP.
The 2025-26 playoffs are partial as of the question date (2026-05-23), so their composition would change.
Whether 'units' means teams, ball-handlers or team-seasons is not specified, and the 70% threshold depends on that choice.
The retrieved records may not include relevant work that exists in other families (not searched further).

historical_effect.explanation: Without history, the question looks like a straightforward unit-level lift test. The retrieved records show that coverage and failure labels are unreliable, that unit-level lifts are noisy and shrink or fail to replicate, and that league-wide effects tend to be play-type-level rather than matchup-specific. This moves the decision to proceed_with_changes, with a pre-registered failure definition, an exposure floor, hierarchical shrinkage, a placebo and split-sample replication, and an explicit allowance for an untestable or inconclusive result.

blocking_constraints.text: 'PNR fail' cannot be taken from coverage labels, which were found sparse (3-15% labeled). It must be defined from play-by-play observables, and that definition is unvalidated.
If failure or PULL_UP is labeled using outcome information (shot result or points), the lift is partly circular.
Per-unit lift SE is likely 4-8pp, so a test of the share of units above 0 is dominated by noise unless units are large or pooled with shrinkage.

prior_work.summary: None of the retrieved families tests PULL_UP after PNR failure. They show the pitfalls of small-n lifts, label sparsity, non-replication and universal-versus-matchup-specific effects, which constrain how the question should be tested.

risks.text: Defining 'failure' or 'PULL_UP' from outcomes makes the lift partly mechanical. Use only pre-shot information, such as the possession state and the action sequence before the shot.

PNR and PULL_UP labels come from play-by-play heuristics (calibrated PNR share is about 18-20% of possessions per FAM:SF-APPM-058). Misclassification would bias lift in unknown directions, and coverage labels are essentially unusable (FAM:SF-APPS-058).

The per-unit SE is large relative to the 2pp median threshold. The share of units above 0 would be about 50% under the null, so the 70% criterion needs a precisely estimated effect, not just a positive sign.
PNR-failure followed by PULL_UP is a small subset of possessions. Many units will fall below any reasonable exposure floor, as seen with n of 15-54 in FAM:SF-APPA-066.
Conditioning on PNR failure, or choosing units by high counter use, invites regression to the mean (FAM:SF-APPA-029 shows near-zero stability of extreme deltas).
Player quality (shooter skill), defender identity, game state, shot clock and shot difficulty confound PULL_UP lift. League-wide high-efficiency play types also inflate lift (FAM:SF-APPA-063 caveat).
Multiple unit definitions, baselines, thresholds and lift metrics would inflate false positives unless fixed in advance.
Without a placebo (for example PULL_UP after non-failed PNR, or other play types after failure), lift may reflect a generic pull-up effect rather than a counter.
League play style and play-by-play logging may shift across 2022-23 to 2025-26 (FAM:SF-APPA-063). Pooling seasons without checks could produce spurious lift.

design.estimand: Within-unit difference in points per possession (and eFG% as secondary), in percentage points, between PULL_UP possessions that follow a pre-registered PNR failure state and the baseline of that unit's PULL_UP possessions after a non-failed PNR, matched on shot clock bucket, game-state bucket, and shooter and defender strata. Secondary summaries: (a) the share of units with lift above 0, and (b) the median lift. Support requires both pre-registered criteria (at least 70% of qualifying units with lift above 0 and median lift above 2pp) to hold in the confirmatory sample AND to exceed the placebo distribution.
design.unit: Offensive team-season as the primary unit. Ball-handler-season is a secondary unit, to be reported separately and not pooled with the primary. Fix the primary unit before analysis.
design.sample: Exploratory/calibration: 2022-23 and 2023-24 regular seasons, used only to fix the PNR-failure definition and the exposure floor. Confirmatory: 2024-25 regular season, with 2025-26 regular season (complete since 2026-04-13) as a second replication. Playoffs are analysed separately as a secondary stratum and not pooled. The partial 2025-26 playoffs are excluded until complete (2026-06-21) and the data version is frozen. PNR failure is defined by play-by-play observables only (e.g. no shot, foul or turnover within N seconds of the screen action, and the possession continues with a second action), and must be validated by manual audit of at least 200 possessions before the confirmatory run.
design.power: Run a pre-analysis variance calculation before looking at lifts: estimate per-unit SE of lift from the number of qualifying possessions. Set a minimum exposure floor (provisionally 100 failure-then-PULL_UP possessions per team-season) and report the number of units passing it. If fewer than 20 units pass, or if the median per-unit SE exceeds 4pp, declare the test untestable at the unit level and use only the pooled hierarchical estimate. Estimate the unit lifts with a hierarchical (random-effects) model and report shrunken lift, the posterior probability of lift above 0 per unit, and the implied share above 0. Report the raw share too, flagged as noise-inflated.
design.controls: Adjust for shot clock, score margin, period, shot distance and location, shooter identity (random effect), defender or matchup minutes where available, and league-season fixed effects. Control for shot quality with a pre-shot expected-points model trained only on other seasons. Do not use outcome-derived labels. Hold the PNR-failure definition fixed once chosen.
design.falsification: Placebo 1: the same lift computed for PULL_UP after non-failed PNR and for other post-failure actions (e.g. drive, pass). Placebo 2: permutation of the failure label within unit-game strata, 1,000 times, to obtain the null distribution of the share-above-0 and median-lift statistics. Placebo 3: lift in a season-lagged split to test persistence (unit-level lift correlation between 2024-25 and 2025-26 halves). Support is void if the placebo distribution reaches the observed statistics at the 5% level, or if split-half unit lift reliability is not meaningfully above 0.
design.multiplicity: A single primary hypothesis with the two-part criterion, one unit definition, one failure definition and one lift metric (PPP). eFG% and ball-handler-season analyses are labeled secondary and Holm-corrected. No threshold tuning after seeing confirmatory data. All variants run are logged and reported.
design.decision_rule: Supported: both criteria met in the 2024-25 confirmatory sample and replicated in 2025-26, with the permutation p<0.05 and placebo lifts near zero. Rejected: adequately powered (floor met, SE under 4pp) and share above 0 below 70% or median lift at or below 2pp, in both seasons. Untestable: exposure or label audit gates failed. Artifact: lift disappears under shot-quality control or matches the placebo. Otherwise uncertain.
design.data_version: Per-game NBA stats API play-by-play, rotation, matchup and box-score files and the derived play-type graph database for 2022-23 through 2025-26 regular seasons, frozen as of 2026-04-13 or later with a recorded hash. Exclude 2025-26 playoffs until complete (2026-06-21), then add as a separate stratum. Record the label pipeline version and any code changes.

research_concepts: pull-up jump shot as counter to PNR coverage
methodological_questions: How should lift in pp be defined and what is the baseline for PULL_UP versus other PNR outcomes?
What is the unit of analysis and the minimum exposure per unit for a stable lift estimate?
How to handle selection and regression to the mean when units are chosen by PNR failure or suppression?
Is the play-type label derived from the outcome, and does this create circularity?
How to set a pre-registered threshold (>=70% of units with lift>0, median lift>2pp) and control multiple testing and confounding by shot quality and defender?
Are there season-to-season stability and placebo checks for counter strategies?
args.query: PNR suppression failure then PULL_UP counter league-wide lift >0 in 70% of units median lift 2pp

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether another tool call is worth it, such as checking the data catalog or searching for PULL_UP, but the budget is fine either way. The terms "PNR fail," "unit," and "lift" are still ambiguous, so I'm leaning toward finalizing now and noting that uncertainty rather than assuming what they mean.

I'm settling on the status labels I'll record, and I'm expecting the outcome to be mostly ambiguous: the "70% of units with positive lift and median over 2pp" criterion would likely come out near chance under noise, and the lift definition is circular. I'm also thinking about how to define "PNR fail" precisely, since the coverage labels in the data look unreliable.

I'm working out how to define the proxy and the lift: PPP or eFG on PULL_UP possessions after a PNR failure, compared against a baseline. For a team-season the sample is small enough that the standard error sits near 4pp, so a per-unit median test won't detect much. I'm leaning toward a hierarchical shrinkage model, checked with split-half reliability and a cross-season holdout, and I'm freezing the 2025-26 data so the incomplete playoffs don't leak in.
